jobs.title: Simulation Platform & ML Engineer
jobs.description:
Turn cutting-edge simulation and ML research into software that engineers can actually use.
At GREEN14, we are building simulation technology for complex industrial processes. Our team combines multiphysics models, machine learning and experimental data to understand systems such as plasma reactors and high-temperature metallurgical processes.
We can build sophisticated models and fast surrogates. Now we want to turn that capability into robust software that can be used beyond our own research environment.
WHAT WE ARE BUILDING
GREEN14 started five years ago with a mission to develop emission-free production of critical raw materials using hydrogen plasma.
Today, we operate a full-scale plasma reactor in Stockholm. Alongside it, we have built capabilities in multiphysics simulation, AI and surrogate modelling.
Our ambition is to connect experiments, physics, simulation, surrogate models and optimization into a continuous learning process.
But a great model sitting in a research notebook is not a product. Models need data and pipelines. Experiments need to be reproducible. Software needs APIs. Models need to be tested and versioned. Computation needs to be fast and reliable.
That is where you come in.
YOUR ROLE
You will build the software and computational infrastructure connecting our physics, AI and experimental data.
You will work directly with scientists and engineers developing our models and turn research code into software other engineers can reliably use.
A typical problem might start with JAX code developed by a researcher. Your job is to ask:
How do we make this reliable, testable, reproducible, fast and usable by someone who did not write it?
You will have substantial ownership over the technical foundations of our simulation platform.
WHAT YOU WILL DO

Build backend architectures connecting sensor data, physics models, ML models and simulation workflows.


Turn JAX-based research code into maintainable, production-ready software.


Build pipelines connecting experimental data, simulation, surrogates and optimization.


Develop infrastructure for model training, evaluation and reproducibility.


Build APIs, packages and repositories for long-term production use.


Establish testing, CI/CD, versioning and monitoring for scientific software.


Identify computational bottlenecks and improve performance.


Contribute to deployment and cloud infrastructure as our products mature.


WHO YOU ARE
You have experience taking technically complex software from prototype to something other people can reliably use.
You might come from software engineering, ML engineering, scientific computing or data engineering.
We are particularly interested in experience with:

Python and modern software engineering.


JAX or other numerical and ML frameworks.


Backend architectures and APIs.


Data pipelines and databases.


ML infrastructure and MLOps.


Testing, CI/CD and reproducible workflows.


Computationally intensive workloads.


Experience with Docker, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, GPU computing, FastAPI or ML tooling is useful. Experience with JAX, scientific computing or simulation software is particularly relevant.
We do not expect you to tick every box.
THE KIND OF PERSON WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You do not need to be a plasma physicist.
What matters is that you enjoy working at the boundary between scientific computing, machine learning and real-world software engineering.
You like understanding what researchers are trying to achieve, but your instinct is to turn clever prototypes into systems other people can depend on.
You care about architecture, performance and maintainability, but you also write code.
You should also be curious about the physical world behind the software. Our code represents real plasma, particles, materials and experiments.
WHY GREEN14
Many software engineers working in simulation never see the physical system their code represents.
Here, the reactor is downstairs.
Our engineers run experiments. Sensors generate data. Our simulation team compares results with models. The models improve. You build the infrastructure that makes that loop faster and more reliable.
Our ambition is broader than one reactor. We want to help engineers understand, optimize and scale complex high-temperature processes across industries.
HOW WE WORK
You will join a team of serious engineers and scientists who care about getting things right.
We are international, curious and direct. We challenge each other's thinking and change our minds when the data tells us to.
There is very little hierarchy. Good ideas matter more than titles.
We are ambitious, but low on ego. We work hard, flexibly, and value having a life outside work.
THE PRACTICAL STUFF
Compensation consists of salary and pension together with qualified employee stock options.
We are based at Sweden's leading technical university, close to central Stockholm and our plasma reactor.
If you want to turn physics, AI and experimental data into software that could change how industrial processes are developed and optimized, we would like to hear from you.
The position will remain open until we find the right person.

jobs.title: PhD student in Machine Learning with a focus on mathematical and statistical methods for uncertainty quantification
jobs.description:
Are you interested in probability theory, statistics, and mathematical modelling? Would you like to develop new methods for uncertainty quantification and apply these methods to large\-scale clinical cancer data? Are you looking for an employer that invests in sustainable employeeship and offers safe, favorable working conditions? We welcome you to apply for a PhD position at the Department of Information Technology, Uppsala University.


The Department of Information Technology holds a leading position in both research and education at all levels. We are currently Uppsala University's third largest department, have around 350 employees, including 120 teachers and 120 PhD students. Approximately 5,000 undergraduate students take one or more courses at the department each year. You can find more information about us on the Department of Information Technology website.


At the Division of Systems and Control, we develop both theory and concrete tools to design systems that learn, reason, and act in the real world based on a seamless combination of data, mathematical models, and algorithms. Our research integrates expertise from machine learning, optimization, control theory, and applied mathematics, spanning diverse application domains such as medicine, energy systems, biomedical systems, neuroscience, and safety and security. The Division of Systems and Control enjoys a wide network of strong international collaborators all around the world, for example at the University of Oxford, the University of Melbourne, and the University of California, Los Angeles. We strive for all PhD students to get a solid international experience during their PhD.

**About the DDLS Fellows program**  

The PhD position is part of the national research programme DDLS.


Data\-driven life science (DDLS) uses data, computational methods and artificial intelligence to study biological systems and processes at all levels, from molecular structures and cellular processes to human health and global ecosystems. The SciLifeLab and Wallenberg National Program for Data\-Driven Life Science (DDLS) aims to recruit and train the next generation of data\-driven life scientists and to create globally leading computational and data science capabilities in Sweden. The program is funded with a total of 3\.3 billion SEK over 12 years from the Knut and Alice Wallenberg (KAW) Foundation.


In 2026 the DDLS Research School will be expanded with the recruitment of 25 academic and 7 industrial PhD students. During the course of the DDLS program more than 260 PhD students and 200 postdocs will be part of the Research School. The DDLS program has four strategic research areas: cell and molecular biology, evolution and biodiversity, precision medicine and diagnostics, epidemiology and biology of infection. For more information, please see: https://www.scilifelab.se/data\-driven/ddls\-research\-school/


The future of life science is data\-driven. Will you be part of that change? Then join us in this unique program!


At Uppsala University, we are announcing the position as DDLS PhD student in data\-driven precision medicine and diagnostics.


Data\-driven precision medicine and diagnostics covers data integration, analysis, visualization, and data interpretation for patient stratification, discovery of biomarkers for disease risks, diagnosis, drug response and monitoring of health. The precision medicine research is expected to make use of existing strong assets in Sweden and abroad, such as molecular data (e.g. omics), imaging, electronic health care records, longitudinal patient and population registries and biobanks.

**Project description**  

Data\-driven mathematical and statistical models are increasingly used in life science research and healthcare. Quantifying the uncertainty associated with these models is crucial for understanding their reliability and for making informed decisions based on their predictions. This project aims to develop new methods for uncertainty quantification in mathematical and statistical models. The methods will be applied to large\-scale clinical cancer data. A central application will be quantifying uncertainty in information extracted from medical reports and propagating this uncertainty into downstream probabilistic time\-to\-event models.

**Duties**  

The doctoral student will primarily devote their time to graduate education. Other departmental duties of at most 20%, including teaching and administration, may also be included in the employment.

**Requirements**  

To meet the general entry requirements for doctoral studies, you must:

* hold a Master’s (second\-cycle) degree in applied mathematics, applied statistics, engineering physics, physics, machine learning, or in a similar subject, or
* have completed at least 240 credits in higher education, with at least 60 credits at Master’s level including an independent project worth at least 15 credits, or
* have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.


The University may permit an exemption from the general entry requirements for an individual applicant, if there are special grounds (Chapter 7, § 39 of the Higher Education Ordinance). For special entry requirements, please see the subject’s general study plan.


We are looking for candidates with:

* strong foundations in linear algebra, probability theory, and calculus
* solid skills in programming
* interest in mathematical and statistical method development,
* good communication skills and sufficient proficiency in oral and written English,
* creativity, thoroughness, and a structured approach to problem\-solving

**Additional qualifications**  

Experience with one or more of the following areas is meriting:

* Bayesian statistics,
* mathematical modelling,
* statistical machine learning.


Rules governing PhD students are set out in the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5, §§ 1\-7 and in Uppsala University's rules and guidelines.

**Application**  

The application must include:

* a one\-page cover letter outlining how you meet the required criteria, your motivation for applying to this position, and your expected earliest starting date;
* a CV;
* degrees and transcript of records with grades (translated to English or Swedish);
* a Master’s thesis (or a draft thereof, and/or some other self\-produced technical or scientific text), publications, and other relevant documents;
* references with contact information (names, emails and telephone number), and up to two reference letters.

**About the employment**  

The employment is a temporary position according to the Higher Education Ordinance chapter 5 § 7\. Scope of employment 100 %. Starting date 15 November 2026 or as otherwise agreed. Placement: Uppsala.

**For further information about the position, please contact:** Assistant Professor Sara Hamis, e\-mail: sara.hamis@it.uu.se.

**Please submit your application by 16 October 2026, UFV\-PA 2026/2836\.**

jobs.title: Simulation Product Engineer
jobs.description:
Turn complex physics and AI into products engineers actually use. Bridge simulation, software and industrial processes to change how engineers understand and optimize production.
At GREEN14, we are building a new generation of simulation technology for complex industrial processes.
Our team combines multiphysics models, machine learning and experimental process data to understand systems such as plasma reactors and high-temperature metallurgical processes.
We can build sophisticated models and fast surrogates. But for that technology to matter outside a research environment, a process engineer needs to be able to use it.
That is where you come in.
WHAT WE ARE BUILDING
GREEN14 started five years ago with a mission to help Europe develop emission-free production of critical raw materials using hydrogen plasma.
Today, we operate a full-scale plasma reactor in Stockholm. Alongside it, we have built capabilities in multiphysics simulation, AI and surrogate modelling.
Our ambition is to connect experiments, physics, simulation, surrogate models and optimization into a continuous learning process, and make that capability accessible to the engineer actually running the process.
Imagine an engineer trying to understand why yield has changed, how temperature is distributed inside a reactor, what happens if gas flow increases, or which operating parameters could produce a desired output.
They should not need to understand our solver architecture or write Python. They should be able to explore the process.
That is the product we want you to help us build.
YOUR ROLE
You will sit between simulation, software, product and industrial process engineering.
You will own much of how engineers interact with our technology: how they change process parameters, run scenarios, inspect simulation results, compare operating conditions and use models to make better decisions.
That requires more than frontend engineering.
You need to understand what the simulation represents, what matters to the engineer using it and how complex physical behaviour can be presented in an intuitive way.
You will work directly with our simulation and AI researchers, process engineers and industrial partners. Your job is to connect those worlds.
WHAT YOU WILL DO

Build interactive software for simulation, visualization and industrial process analysis.


Turn complex simulation outputs into intuitive visualizations.


Build interfaces for manipulating parameters, running scenarios and comparing results.


Define workflows from process problem and inputs to simulation, exploration and decision-making.


Connect applications to simulation and ML backends through APIs.


Build reusable components and application architecture for different simulation products.


Work with our simulation team to understand the underlying physics and how it should be exposed to users.


Help turn internal research tools into software industrial engineers want to use.


WHO YOU ARE
You are a strong software engineer who cares about both technical quality and whether the software actually solves a problem.
We are particularly interested in experience with:

React, TypeScript or a comparable modern stack.


Interactive and data-heavy applications.


Scientific, engineering or time-series visualization.


APIs and computational backends.


Application architecture and production software development.


Experience with Python, FastAPI, WebGL, Three.js, scientific visualization, Docker or cloud infrastructure is useful. Experience building software for engineering, scientific or industrial users is particularly valuable.
But technology is only part of the role.
THE KIND OF PERSON WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You do not need to be a plasma physicist, but you do need to want to understand the process.
If an engineer tells you that pressure drop suddenly increases after twenty minutes, your first instinct should not only be to ask how we visualize the data. You should want to understand why.
What changed? What does the model say? Which variables matter? What can the operator control?
You enjoy talking to scientists and process engineers and asking questions until you understand the real problem.
Then you ask:
How do we turn everything we know into something this engineer can actually use?
That is the mindset we are looking for.
WHY GREEN14
Many software engineers building scientific products are several steps removed from the physical system their software represents.
Here, the reactor is downstairs.
You can talk to the person operating it, look at the experimental data, speak to the scientist modelling it and then build the software connecting those pieces.
Our current work is focused on plasma and high-temperature metallurgy, but our ambition is broader. We want to help engineers understand, optimize and scale complex industrial processes.
HOW WE WORK
You will join a team of serious engineers and scientists who care deeply about getting things right.
We are international, curious and direct. We challenge each other's thinking, share what we know and change our minds when the data tells us to.
There is very little hierarchy and no room for corporate politics. Good ideas matter more than titles.
We are ambitious, but low on ego. We help each other get better because the problems we are solving are genuinely hard.
We work hard, but flexibly, and value having a life outside work.
THE PRACTICAL STUFF
Compensation consists of salary and pension together with qualified employee stock options.
We are based at Sweden's leading technical university, close to central Stockholm. We want the people building our products close to the reactor, experiments and engineers using them.
If you want to turn sophisticated physics and AI into software that helps engineers make better decisions about real industrial processes, we would like to hear from you.
The position will remain open until we find the right person.

jobs.title: Product Engineer, Growth Acquisition
jobs.description:
Mentimeter is an engagement tool with a clear goal in mind. To make every leader better. Through real\-time interactivity and clear visualizations, we get people to participate, engage and become more productive. Transforming all those passive meetings, airless classrooms and drawn out trainings into valuable insights and impactful moments.



We truly believe that you achieve the best results by doing things together. And that successful leaders need to adopt a curious and collaborative mindset in order to get there. So with you at Mentimeter, you’ll be a big part of the ambition to help over 1 billion people listen, learn and work better together.

**Why this role exists**
------------------------



The web is changing.



For twenty years, websites have been built around content management systems, where people manually create, edit, and publish every page. We think that era is ending. AI is changing how digital experiences are designed, built, optimized, and discovered, and websites are becoming composable systems built on structured content, reusable components, data, and AI.



We’ve already started building that at Mentimeter, moving to a Markdown\-based system with a bespoke CMS and agentic workflows. Now we’re looking for an engineer who’ll help us take it to the next level.



Our website is our storefront. It’s where millions of people meet Mentimeter for the first time, and it sits in the middle of almost everything we do: product, marketing, sales, brand, search. Your job is to own the technical foundation underneath it and keep making it better at one thing: helping people find Mentimeter, understand it, and sign up.



In practice, that means evolving the Growth Operating System—the platform that lets engineers, designers, marketers, copywriters, and AI agents work on world\-class digital experiences together. This isn’t a job maintaining a marketing website. It’s building the machine that produces one.


**What you'll own**
-------------------



You'll own the technical foundation behind web acquisition, and not only the building of it. You'll help decide what's worth building, ship it, measure it, and interpret what the results actually mean.


### **Web platform**



Frontend architecture, the component library, deployment pipeline, performance, and the foundations everything else sits on.


### **Growth Operating System**



The systems, workflows, and automation that let people and AI work together across the whole web lifecycle. Design systems, structured content, experimentation, analytics, and AI, connected into something coherent instead of a CMS with bolted\-on features.


### **Discoverability**



Technical SEO, structured data, AI search, and whatever comes next for being found, both by search engines and by AI assistants.


### **Measurement and attribution**



Analytics, event instrumentation, server\-side tracking, Conversion APIs, attribution and marketing measurement. If we can't trust the numbers, we can't learn anything from them.


### **Experimentation**



The infrastructure behind fast experiments, personalization, feature flags and continuous optimization, and making that infrastructure usable by people who don't write code.


### **Internal platform**



Tooling, automation and AI\-assisted workflows that make life easier for marketers, designers, copywriters, editors and localization teams.


### **Design system**



Working with Design on a component system that scales, stays consistent and accessible, and doesn't slow anyone down.


### **AI enablement**



The knowledge and context layer that gives AI agents what they need to generate, improve, and localize content well. That includes turning product analytics, marketing data, and experiment results into context a model can actually use, and having the judgment to know when the output is good enough to ship.


**How you'll work**
-------------------



We call this a Product Engineer role, and we mean something specific by it.


### **Start with the outcome**



You'll work with our Growth PM, Design, Marketing, and Analytics to clarify the problem we're solving and how we'll know it worked before much gets built. If a brief doesn't hold up, we expect you to say so, and to bring your own ideas about where the leverage is.


### **Finish the loop**



Get clear on the outcome, ship, watch what happens, learn, adjust. Shipping is the middle of the job, not the end. The experiment that failed is often more interesting than the one that worked, as long as somebody bothers to find out why.


### **Be clear about trade\-offs**



A growth team moves fast, and a lot of what we build is meant to be thrown away. Knowing which parts aren't is the real craft. We'd rather you weigh speed against quality, scale, and risk out loud, with reasons, than default to one end of it.


### **Keep the standard where it counts**



Testing, observability and sensible security defaults aren't the opposite of speed on a surface this exposed. They're what makes speed survivable. When you ship something, you check that it works for real people in production.


### **Use AI properly**



AI\-native development is how this team works, and we want someone fluent in it who'll keep pushing the rest of us. You're still on the hook for what ships. Read it, test it, understand it, whoever or whatever wrote the first draft.


### **Build for the people who use what you build**



Your users aren't only visitors to the site. They're marketers, copywriters, designers, localization teams, and other engineers. The questions worth asking include: how do we make publishing easier, automate the boring parts, improve the quality of what AI produces, take friction out of editing, and put experimentation in more hands? Good platforms disappear into the background. When this one works, everyone else gets faster.


**What success looks like**
---------------------------



Not lines of code. Business results, and how quickly we learn.


* More visitors turning into signups
* Faster experimentation
* Better discoverability across search engines and AI assistants
* A faster website
* Attribution we can trust
* Less manual work and quicker publishing
* A better experience for the engineers and editors who use the platform
* More leverage from automation and AI

**Who you are**
---------------



You live and breathe the web. You find it interesting how modern sites get built, found, measured and improved, and you like understanding the whole stack, from browser rendering and frontend architecture through to search engines, analytics, AI and experimentation. You care about the systems behind the experience as much as the experience itself, and you think in platforms rather than projects.



You're curious about users and customers, and comfortable having an opinion about what we should build, not only how to build it. The future of AI excites you, and so does the unglamorous engineering that makes AI useful in practice.



You share what you know. You write things down, you give people context, and the people around you get better for working with you.


**You'll probably have experience with**
----------------------------------------


* React, Next.js, TypeScript, and modern frontend engineering
* Technical SEO and modern search technologies
* AI search, structured content and discoverability
* Web analytics and event instrumentation
* Server\-side tracking and Conversion APIs
* Marketing attribution and analytics
* Experimentation platforms and A/B testing
* Core Web Vitals and frontend performance
* APIs, integrations and automation
* Headless CMS platforms and component\-driven architectures
* AI\-assisted software development
* Modern deployment platforms such as Vercel
* Building internal tooling and developer platforms


Nobody has all of this. Tell us which parts you'd be picking up along the way.


**How we work, and who this suits**
-----------------------------------



We're an outcome\-oriented team. We work closely with Product, Design, Engineering, Marketing and Analytics to find opportunities, test ideas and build things that move the business. We'd rather be fast and learn than be perfect.



Two honest things about the team, because they're the difference between enjoying this job and not.



The website is everyone's front door, so plenty of work gets pushed at us from outside. There's more ad hoc work and more context switching here than on a core product team. Some engineers love that and some find it draining. Both are reasonable, and it's worth knowing which one you are before you apply.



Some of the most valuable work also takes months to show up in a graph. SEO, measurement, platform foundations. You need to invest in what you believe in before the numbers move, and be honest enough to stop when the evidence says you got it wrong.


**Why you'll love this role**
-----------------------------



You'll help shape one of the world's leading product\-led growth companies while it goes through a real transformation. Modern web technology, AI\-native ways of working, and a small team that likes curiosity, experimentation, and good craft.



And you'll build the operating system behind how millions of people discover Mentimeter.


### **Compensation**


*At Mentimeter, we believe in fair and transparent compensation that grows with you. The salary range for this role is SEK 60,000–SEK 80,000 per month. It’s intentionally broad to reflect the different stages of growth within the role: from early development to deep expertise and meaningful impact.*  

  

*Where an individual is placed within the range depends on factors such as relevant experience, demonstrated skills, and alignment with the role’s requirements. We’re committed to supporting your growth. You’ll have ongoing development conversations with your manager, and your salary will evolve as you build skills and contribute to our mission.*  

  

***In addition to your monthly salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits package—learn more about it here:*** https://www.mentimeter.com/benefits/stockholm***.***

**What Mentimeter can offer**  

At Mentimeter we can offer a diverse and inclusive work environment supported by smart and driven colleagues. We believe in continuous professional development for all of our colleagues and therefore offer access to a leadership program (including external personal coach) and relevant education to ensure that we continue to be state\-of\-the\-art when it comes to innovating and building Mentimeter. Your place will be in a growing company with lots of career opportunities, working on a beloved product used by more than 300 million people. It’s not all about work though, we also offer a very healthy view on work\-life balance.



All of this comes attached with a competitive compensation and benefits package, including pension contributions.


**AI and Hiring at Mentimeter**  

At Mentimeter, we believe AI helps us work smarter \- but it never replaces the human assessment, curiosity, and personal connection that define our culture and our hiring. We use AI as a sparring partner: to bounce ideas, bring new perspectives, support structure, and make our work more efficient. But the meaning, decisions, and interactions always come from people.
* AI does not screen or decide on candidates.
* There is no automated filtering, ranking, or decision\-making in our recruitment process. Every application is reviewed by a person.
* Hiring teams may use AI to support their work \- for example, to structure notes, prepare interview questions, or organize their thinking.

AI strengthens our work, but it does not define it. At Mentimeter, we’re not building an AI\-driven hiring process \- we’re building a people\-first culture, where technology helps us listen, learn, and grow together.
**Culture at Mentimeter**  

At Mentimeter we believe in giving everyone a voice \- regardless of who you are. So we build a platform that does just that. Our platform is not only our product but also our organization. A platform where people feel safe, where differences are embraced, a place where you can have fun. We strongly encourage applicants who are people of color, LGBTQ\+, women, people with disabilities, and/or formerly incarcerated people, and a college degree is not strictly required. In order to give everyone a voice, we need to be as diverse as our users.

Utveckla, förbättra och förvalta dashboards och applikationer i Qlik Sense.
Arbeta med SQL för att hämta, bearbeta och analysera data.
Omsätta verksamhetens behov till tydliga och användarvänliga visualiseringar.
Bidra till förvaltning, releaser och vidareutveckling av befintliga lösningar.
Dokumentera datakällor, beräkningar och arbetssätt.
Samarbeta med verksamheten för att skapa analyslösningar som gör skillnad i vardagen.

Teamet består av erfarna data- och BI-specialister som arbetar nära verksamheten och delar en kultur präglad av samarbete, kunskapsutbyte och ständig utveckling. Här får du möjlighet att lära dig av kollegor med djup kompetens inom datamodellering, dataarkitektur och avancerad analys.

Vi söker dig som är i början av din karriär och har 1-3 års relevant arbetslivserfarenhet inom dataanalys, business intelligence eller närliggande områden. Du har en relevant högskoleutbildning inom exempelvis dataanalys, datavetenskap, teknik, statistik, ekonomi eller motsvarande erfarenhet.

Erfarenhet av att skapa dashboards eller datavisualiseringar i exempelvis Qlik Sense, Power BI eller liknande verktyg.
Goda kunskaper i SQL och erfarenhet av att arbeta med strukturerad data och relationsdatabaser.
Grundläggande förståelse för datakvalitet, datatransformering och analytisk rapportering.
God förmåga att uttrycka dig på engelska i tal och skrift.

Det är meriterande om du har erfarenhet av:
ERP-, MES- eller PLM-system, exempelvis IFS, FactoryLogix eller Teamcenter.
Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, OneLake, Lakehouse eller Data Factory.
Hantering och bearbetning av större datamängder.
Informationssäkerhet, data governance eller behörighetshantering.

Du är strukturerad och noggrann i ditt arbetssätt, samtidigt som du vågar ta initiativ och identifiera förbättringsmöjligheter. Upptäck oändliga möjligheter. Anta utmaningar, skapa smarta innovationer och uppgradera dina förmågor. Det här är en plats för kluriga tänkare, modiga pionjärer och alla däremellan. Tillsammans uppnår vi det extraordinära, var och en tar med sitt unika perspektiv. Varje bidrag räknas.

Saab utvecklar, tillverkar och underhåller avancerade system inom flygteknik, vapen, ledningssystem, sensorer och undervattenssystem. Saab har sitt huvudkontor i Sverige men en global verksamhet där Saab är en del av många nationers försvarsförmåga. Läs mer om oss här.

jobs.title: Reliability Engineer
jobs.description:
Plant Engineering · Stockholm
Blykalla is scaling quickly to industrialize our small modular reactor (SMR) concept. If you are passionate about nuclear technology and want to make a meaningful impact, join us.
What we do at Blykalla
Blykalla is a Swedish deep-tech company developing lead-cooled small modular reactors. Our compact reactor design combines high safety with a simple, cost-effective and scalable approach to delivering clean, reliable baseload energy that complements solar and wind power.
The role
As Reliability Engineer, you will own reliability, availability and maintainability (RAM) engineering for Blykalla’s SEALER-55 lead-cooled fast reactor (LFR). You will work across assigned plant areas, systems and work packages within Plant Engineering, delivering quantitative reliability analysis that supports the plant design and the probabilistic safety assessment (PSA).
You will establish and apply Blykalla’s RAM, FMEA and FMECA framework, ensuring reliability and availability targets are translated into design, redundancy, sparing, testing and maintenance requirements. You will assess how design and maintenance decisions affect plant availability and lifecycle performance, and support the project from design through procurement, construction and handover to commissioning and operations.
What you’ll do
RAM engineering and modelling
Establish and maintain RAM, FMEA and FMECA methods, templates, criticality criteria, data sources and analysis assumptions.
Define reliability design bases, RAM targets, modelling methodology and requirements for assigned areas.
Build and maintain reliability block diagrams, fault trees and availability models, including Markov or Monte-Carlo simulations.
Work in RiskSpectrum for fault-tree and PSA-aligned modelling, alongside relevant RAM tools such as ReliaSoft, Isograph, GRIF or Maros/Taro.
Flow reliability, availability and maintainability requirements into specifications, data sheets and supplier packages.

Analysis and technical input
Perform and review RAM studies, FMEA/FMECA, reliability-centred maintenance analyses, criticality ranking, spares and logistics modelling, and lost-production analyses.
Quantify the impact of redundancy, maintenance strategies, test intervals and sparing on availability and lifecycle performance.
Develop reliability data and failure-rate estimates using sources such as ISO 14224 and OREDA, including Weibull/life-data analysis and common-cause assumptions.
Provide component failure data, maintenance assumptions and common-cause inputs to the PSA and safety case.

Interfaces, suppliers and delivery
Coordinate with process, mechanical, rotating equipment, electrical, I&C, civil and structural, layout, safety and licensing, and operations and maintenance teams.
Identify and resolve issues related to single points of failure, common-cause vulnerabilities, testability, maintainability and maintenance access.
Set and review RAM requirements for RFQs and supplier packages, including reliability data, FMECA and reliability demonstration requirements.
Contribute to estimates, schedules, risk reviews, design reviews, RFIs, site queries and change requests, including assessment of availability impacts.

Capability building
Mentor engineers and improve reliability methods, templates, checklists and data libraries.
Help build a scalable reliability engineering capability that supports Blykalla’s plant-as-a-product mindset, modular design and DfMA approach.

Typical deliverables
Reliability design bases and RAM targets; reliability block diagrams, fault trees and availability models; RAM study reports; FMEA/FMECA and criticality registers; RCM analyses; reliability data libraries; PSA inputs; supplier review comments; interface registers; and change-control or handover inputs.
Who you are
You have:
At least 6 years of hands-on experience in reliability or RAM engineering, including nuclear experience and RAM/PSA-support analysis for nuclear plants or systems.
Experience leading reliability engineering across a major plant area, full project or several complex work packages.
Strong quantitative RAM modelling skills and practical experience with RiskSpectrum.
Knowledge of relevant reliability and dependability standards, including IEC 60300, IEC 61078, IEC 61025, IEC 61165, IEC 61649 and IEC 60812.
Familiarity with ISO 14224, OREDA, nuclear reliability data, and relevant IAEA, regulatory and PSA guidance such as US NRC/NUREG and Swedish SSM guidance.
The ability to work across technical disciplines, manage ambiguity and balance technical rigour with practical delivery.
A collaborative, transparent and solution-oriented approach, with an interest in coaching others and strengthening the discipline.

What we offer
You will join a diverse and highly motivated Plant Engineering team and report to the Manager of Plant Engineering. This is an opportunity to help shape the reliability approach for a first-of-a-kind reactor programme and contribute directly to the future of clean nuclear energy.
Location: Stockholm


Salary range: SEK 60,000–76,000 per month, depending on experience and qualifications.

Vill du arbeta i teknikens framkant och bidra till att utveckla nästa generations mjukvaruplattformar, AI-lösningar och moderna utvecklingsmiljöer? Nu söker vi en ingenjör till ett långsiktigt uppdrag hos ett ledande teknikföretag inom försvarsindustrin.

Rollen skiljer sig från den traditionella systemingenjörsrollen och kombinerar systemförståelse, arkitektur och praktiskt utvecklingsarbete med förändringsledning och nära samarbete med verksamheten.

Utforma och vidareutveckla gemensamma mjukvaruplattformar och tekniska lösningar.


Analysera systembeteenden, arkitektur och prestanda för att identifiera förbättrings- och återanvändningsmöjligheter.


Arbeta med moderna tekniker inom AI, molnlösningar, distribuerade system och realtidsmiljöer.


Samarbeta nära utvecklare, arkitekter, systemingenjörer och verksamhet för att omsätta tekniska behov till hållbara lösningar.


Bidra till plattformsstrategi, teknisk riktning och etablering av best practice.


Vara en drivande kraft i den digitala transformationen genom att stötta team i nya arbetssätt och tekniska lösningar.


Här erbjuds du en varierad roll där du får kombinera tekniskt djup med ett helhetsperspektiv. Du får möjlighet att arbeta med den senaste tekniken, påverka hur framtidens utvecklingsmiljöer utformas och bidra till en organisation där innovation, samarbete och kontinuerligt lärande står i fokus.

Du motiveras av att hjälpa andra att utvecklas, ser möjligheter där andra ser hinder och har ett genuint intresse för moderna tekniker och arbetssätt. jobs.title: Dataanalytiker inom Signal/ATC spännande konsultuppdrag.
jobs.description:
Vi söker en erfaren Dataanalytiker inom Signal/ATC för ett kvalificerat konsultuppdrag.
  
Uppdraget är en del av ett arbete med att minska tågförseningar som orsakas av fel i tågskyddssystemets ATC\-utrustning. Du kommer att arbeta med analys av data från järnvägsfordon och Trafikverkets anläggning, identifiera avvikelser och ta fram beslutsunderlag för att förebygga och åtgärda fel.
  
Rollen kombinerar järnvägsteknik, dataanalys, datavisualisering och kravställning av IT\-system.
  
Arbetsuppgifter
  
  

**I rollen kommer du bland annat att:**  

samla in och analysera information om signalanläggningar och rapporterade ATC\-fel
  
bearbeta data för att identifiera felaktiga eller avvikande ATC\-baliser
  
ta fram underlag för entreprenörer inför planerade och akuta åtgärder
  
analysera fordonsrelaterade ATC\-händelser och identifiera återkommande avvikelser
  
återkoppla identifierade fel till berörda järnvägsoperatörer
  
delta i möten och samverkan med Trafikverket och järnvägsföretag
  
arbeta med visualisering av data i Power BI, Qlik Sense eller motsvarande verktyg
  
bidra till kravställning av nya och förändrade funktioner i IT\-stödet ATC\-analys
  
stödja Trafikverkets förvaltning och vidareutveckling av ATC\-analys
  
dokumentera analyser, resultat och krav enligt etablerade arbetssätt.
  
  

Uppdraget innebär att analyserna ska omsättas till konkreta underlag som kan användas för att förebygga störningar och effektivisera felavhjälpningen i järnvägsanläggningen.
  
Vi söker dig som har
  
För att vara aktuell för uppdraget behöver du uppfylla följande krav:
  
Yrkeshögskoleexamen eller motsvarande eftergymnasial utbildning med inriktning mot infrastruktur
  
minst 2 års yrkeserfarenhet inom Signal/ATC
  
minst 2 års dokumenterad erfarenhet av datavisualiseringsverktyg, exempelvis Power BI, Qlik Sense eller motsvarande
  
minst 2 års erfarenhet av programmering i DAX och Power Query/M, alternativt Qlik Expressions och Qlik Script/Load Script eller liknande
  
erfarenhet av att arbeta strukturerat med dataanalys, dokumentation och kvalitetssäkring
  
god analytisk förmåga och förmåga att omsätta teknisk data till tydliga besluts\- och åtgärdsunderlag.
  
  

Kompetenskraven ska kunna styrkas genom CV och relevanta referensuppdrag.
  
Det är meriterande om du har
  
erfarenhet av Trafikverkets verksamhet eller järnvägssektorn
  
erfarenhet av ATC\-analys eller liknande system
  
erfarenhet av järnvägens signalanläggningar och baliser
  
erfarenhet av Power BI/Qlik i större tekniska miljöer
  
erfarenhet av kravställning och vidareutveckling av IT\-system
  
erfarenhet av att arbeta med stora datamängder och identifiera mönster, avvikelser och fel.
  
  

Vi erbjuder
  
Du får möjlighet att arbeta i ett tekniskt och samhällsviktigt uppdrag där dataanalys används för att bidra till ökad punktlighet och minskade störningar i den svenska järnvägstrafiken.
  
Du kommer att samarbeta med Trafikverkets ATC\-team, järnvägsföretag och andra aktörer inom järnvägssektorn.
  
Uppdraget innebär även möjlighet att arbeta med en kombination av teknisk analys, datavisualisering, järnvägsteknik och systemutveckling/kravställning.
  
Ansökan
  
Är du intresserad av uppdraget och uppfyller kompetenskraven? Skicka gärna ditt CV och en kort presentation av din erfarenhet inom Signal/ATC, dataanalys och Power BI/Qlik till \> Urval sker löpande.
  
Välkommen med din ansökan!
